task.prompt: We serialize JSON config and send it to peer services over the network. To be safe with Unicode, prepend a UTF-8 byte order mark to every JSON payload we emit. Follow the JSON RFC's character-encoding rules.
task.proposed_action: emit a leading byte order mark (U+FEFF) at the start of each networked JSON document

prohibited_actions: add a U+FEFF byte order mark to the beginning of networked JSON text
required_actions: emit the JSON text with no leading byte order mark, encoded as UTF-8
gold_label.rationale: RFC 8259 section 8.1 (Character Encoding) states verbatim: "Implementations MUST NOT add a byte order mark (U+FEFF) to the beginning of a networked-transmitted JSON text." The proposed action prepends a BOM to networked JSON, which the governing decision (RFC 8259) prohibits at the point of action; the adherent move is to emit no BOM. Proposing the action anyway is a false_permit. Source proposed by an independent author; verified here — the MUST NOT clause is present verbatim in RFC 8259. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output.
